formation.title: The Swabian Question
formation.text:
The old Duchy of Swabia perished with the last Hohenstaufen, leaving behind a mosaic of free cities, knight-cantons, and princely territories held together only by shared language and common interest. Now that mosaic has been gathered under a single banner, but what kind of Swabia shall this be?

The cities of Augsburg, Ulm, and Memmingen have long governed themselves through councils and guilds, defending their liberties through the Swabian League. Their wealth and collective spirit made this unification possible. Yet there are those who remember that Swabia was once a stem duchy ruled by emperors, and argue that only a strong prince can hold these lands together.

The character of Swabia hangs in the balance: a confederation of free cities and cooperative estates, or a restored duchy with centralized authority.

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are a league of free cities, bound by commerce

modifiers.name: League of Equals
modifiers.text: The cities of Swabia have bound themselves in common cause, pooling their wealth and arms in defense of shared liberties against both princely ambition and imperial overreach.

options.text: Swabia needs a strong duke to lead

modifiers.name: Ducal Restoration
modifiers.text: A strong hand now grasps the fractured duchy, welding its quarrelsome cities and petty lords into a cohesive state under princely authority, reviving the martial traditions of the Hohenstaufen.

advances.name: Hohenstaufen Legacy
advances.text: The memory of the great Staufer dynasty (Frederick Barbarossa, Henry VI, Frederick II) lends prestige and cultural weight to any who claim Swabia as their own.

advances.name: Urban League Tradition
advances.text: The Swabian cities' long practice of binding together in leagues for mutual defense and commercial advantage, from the first league of 1376 to the great alliance of 1488.

advances.name: Fortified Towns
advances.text: Swabian free cities invested heavily in walls, towers, and militia training to protect their liberties against princely aggression.

advances.name: Fustian Industry
advances.text: The weaving of fustian (a blend of cotton and linen) made Augsburg and Ulm the textile capitals of the Empire, with production reaching ten thousand pieces annually.

advances.name: Imperial Knights of Swabia
advances.text: The Swabian knight-cantons maintained a military tradition independent of any prince, owing allegiance directly to the Emperor.

advances.name: Fugger Banking
advances.text: The Fugger family of Augsburg built the most powerful banking house in Europe, financing Habsburgs and popes through innovative credit secured against mining concessions.

event.title: The House of Fugger
event.text:
What began as a modest weaving workshop in Augsburg has grown into the most powerful banking house in Christendom. The Fuggers (first Hans, then his sons and grandsons) leveraged the textile trade into a financial empire spanning from the silver mines of Tyrol to the copper fields of Hungary. Their counting houses extend credit to popes and emperors alike.

Jakob Fugger, called 'the Rich,' has secured mining monopolies across central Europe by offering Habsburg princes loans they cannot refuse, accepting mineral rights as collateral. His innovations in double-entry bookkeeping and international credit networks have made Augsburg the banking capital of the Empire.

The Fugger wealth is now inseparable from Swabian prosperity.

options.text: Augsburg shall be the counting house of Europe

modifiers.name: Fugger Patronage
modifiers.text: The vast wealth of the Fugger banking dynasty flows through Augsburg, financing mines, churches, and public works across Swabia.

advances.name: Augsburg Metalworking
advances.text: Augsburg's guild of armorers and weaponsmiths gained renown across Europe for the quality of their plate armor and edged weapons.

advances.name: League Collective Defense
advances.text: The 1488 Swabian League formalized mutual defense among cities, knights, and princes, creating a federal army of 13,000 men governed by a council of three colleges. Every member owed a fixed quota of paid foot.

advances.name: Augsburg Cannon Foundries
advances.text: Augsburg's mastery of bronze and iron casting extended naturally to the production of artillery pieces, supplying siege trains to the League and the Emperor alike.

advances.name: Circle Administration
advances.text: The Imperial Circle system, formalized under Maximilian I, gave Swabia an administrative framework for tax collection, military levies, and keeping the peace.

advances.name: Social Welfare Traditions
advances.text: Jakob Fugger's founding of the Fuggerei in 1521 (the world's first social housing complex) exemplified Swabia's tradition of civic charity and urban welfare.

advances.name: League Warcraft
advances.text: The Swabian League proved its military worth by crushing the Great Peasants' War of 1524-26 and defeating an alliance of robber barons in the Franconian War.

event.title: The League Takes the Field
event.text:
The Swabian League, that great alliance of cities, princes, and knights, has proven itself not merely a diplomatic instrument but a formidable military force. When peasant armies rose across the southwest in revolt against tithes and serfdom, and when robber barons terrorized the trade roads, the League mustered its contingents and marched.

Under the command of Georg Truchsess von Waldburg, the League's army (drawn from dozens of member states, each contributing their quota of pike, horse, and cannon) crushed the rebel forces with methodical efficiency. The collective military capacity of the League has been proven beyond doubt.

options.text: The strength of the League lies in its unity

advances.name: Confessional Coexistence
advances.text: Augsburg's biconfessional governance (Lutherans and Catholics sharing civic offices and church buildings) became a model of practical tolerance in a divided Empire.

event.title: The Peace of Augsburg
event.text:
After decades of religious strife that divided neighbor against neighbor and shattered the old Swabian League, the princes and cities of the Empire have gathered in Augsburg to settle the confessional question. The resulting peace establishes a new principle: the ruler's faith determines the faith of his land.

For Swabia, this moment carries special weight. Augsburg itself has long been home to both confessions, with Lutheran and Catholic communities sharing the same city walls in uneasy coexistence. Some Swabian cities embraced the Reformation early; others remained staunchly Catholic. The peace offers two paths: enforce confessional uniformity to strengthen state authority, or embrace the practical tolerance that Augsburg's own experience has demonstrated.

options.text: Cuius regio, eius religio: one faith, one realm

modifiers.name: Cuius Regio, Eius Religio
modifiers.text: The principle of the Augsburg settlement grants the ruler authority over the faith of his subjects, strengthening central control and religious uniformity.

options.text: Let Augsburg's example guide us toward coexistence

modifiers.name: Augsburg Coexistence
modifiers.text: Augsburg's long tradition of biconfessional governance becomes a model for the realm, fostering tolerance and attracting merchants of all faiths.

advances.name: Fine Cloth Manufactory
advances.text:
The evolution of Swabian textiles from basic fustian to luxury fine cloth, as Augsburg's six thousand weavers refined their craft to compete with Italian and Flemish masters.

Available in: Webhaus

advances.name: Swabian Military Reforms
advances.text: The modernization of the Swabian Circle's military contingents into professional standing forces, trained in the pike-and-shot tactics that the Landsknechte had pioneered.

advances.name: Augsburg Printing Presses
advances.text: Augsburg became one of the leading centers of printing in the Empire, producing religious tracts, commercial manuals, and illustrated books that spread across Europe.

advances.name: Princely Splendor
advances.text: The wealth of Swabia's merchant dynasties and princely houses found expression in magnificent palaces, churches, and art collections that rivaled any in the Empire.

advances.name: Standing Kreis Army
advances.text: The Swabian Circle maintained permanent military forces for defense against French and Ottoman threats, evolving from League contingents into professional standing armies.

advances.name: Commercial Code
advances.text: Swabian cities codified commercial law governing contracts, partnerships, and debt, providing legal certainty that attracted merchants from across Europe.

advances.name: Enlightenment Scholarship
advances.text: The University of Tuebingen and other Swabian institutions became centers of Enlightenment thought, producing philosophers, scientists, and legal scholars of note.

advances.name: Industrial Textiles
advances.text: The mechanization of Swabian textile production, as water-powered mills and early factories transformed the ancient weaving tradition into modern industry.

advances.name: Civic Nationalism
advances.text: Swabia's urban democratic traditions shaped a distinctive form of civic nationalism rooted in self-governance, guild solidarity, and popular sovereignty.

advances.name: Autonomy Heritage
advances.text: Even as Napoleonic mediatization absorbed Swabia's free cities and petty states, the tradition of local autonomy and self-governance persisted in civic institutions.

advances.name: Industrial Modernization
advances.text: Wuerttemberg led Swabia into the industrial age, its metalworking and engineering traditions evolving into modern manufacturing and armaments production.

destiny.name: The Swabian Destiny
destiny.text: Swabia stands united for the first time since the Hohenstaufen. Now it must chart its course: will the league of cities forge a commercial empire, or will a new duke restore the glory of the old stem duchy?

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Swabian Destiny
event.text: The scattered fragments of the old duchy have been gathered into a single hand. Swabia lives again, but the question of what it shall become remains unanswered. The path ahead is long, and the choices we make now will echo through the centuries.

destiny.name: The Handelsverein
destiny.text: Extend Swabian commercial influence along the Rhine by securing Strasbourg and bringing silk into our markets. Requires stability and the League path.

conditions.text: Swabia follows the path of the League of Equals
Own Strasbourg, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25
A market the country is in

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

event.title: The Rhenish Connection
event.text:
The merchants of Augsburg and Ulm have long traded along the Rhine, sending their cloth and metalwork northward to the Low Countries and the Baltic. Now, with Strasbourg in our grasp, the entire upper Rhine corridor lies open to Swabian commerce.

Silk flows through our markets, dyes enrich our workshops, and Fugger silver greases the wheels of trade. The old Swabian League was a defensive alliance, but the Handelsverein we are building is something far more ambitious: a commercial confederation that will bind the cities of central Europe together through shared interest and mutual profit.

options.text: The Rhine shall be our highway

destiny.name: Continental Exchange
destiny.text: Build a trading network spanning from the Rhine to Flanders. Control Bruges, make Augsburg, the city of the Fuggers, the center of its own market, and amass substantial wealth.

conditions.text: Own Bruges, or a subject owns it
We own Augsburg and it is the center of a market
Gold at least 2000

event.title: The Continental Exchange
event.text:
Swabian merchants now trade in the great markets of Flanders, their warehouses in Bruges bulging with cloth, copper, and silver. Augsburg keeps a market of its own now, and its banking houses have transformed it from a provincial weaving town into the financial crossroads of Europe.

The question now is how to consolidate this commercial supremacy. Some argue that Augsburg's spy networks and financial intelligence should be weaponized to outmaneuver rivals. Others believe that an alliance with the Hanseatic cities of the north would create an unassailable trading bloc stretching from the Mediterranean to the Baltic.

options.text: Deploy our agents across every market

modifiers.name: Continental Exchange
modifiers.text: Augsburg's financial intelligence networks span the continent, monitoring markets and manipulating prices to Swabian advantage.

options.text: Forge a partnership with the Hansa

modifiers.name: Hanseatic Partnership
modifiers.text: A formal alliance with the Hanseatic cities creates a trading bloc stretching from the Alps to the Baltic, stabilizing commerce across the region.

destiny.name: Handelshegemonie
destiny.text: Achieve commercial supremacy over Europe by controlling Venice, reaching the highest prestige, amassing vast capital, and seeing Augsburg grow into the counting house of the continent.

conditions.text: Own Venice, or a subject owns it
Prestige at least 75
We own Augsburg and its development is at least 54
Gold at least 3000

event.title: The Handelshegemonie
event.text:
Venice has fallen under Swabian influence, and with it the last great independent trading power of Europe. From the textile halls of Augsburg to the lagoons of the Adriatic, from the counting houses of Bruges to the silk markets of the East, Swabian capital flows through the veins of European commerce.

This unprecedented commercial dominion raises a fundamental question about the nature of the Swabian state. Shall the great merchant families (the Fuggers, the Welsers, the Hochstetters) formally take the reins of government as merchant princes? Or shall the markets remain truly free, open to all comers, with no single dynasty able to corner trade?

options.text: Let the great houses govern as they trade

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes
modifiers.text: The great Swabian merchant dynasties govern as they trade, with calculation, ambition, and an eye toward innovation.

options.text: Free markets serve all, not merely the few

modifiers.name: Free Market Republic
modifiers.text: Swabia's markets remain open to all comers, fostering competition, tolerance, and peaceful prosperity.

destiny.name: The Stauferreich
destiny.text: Reclaim the heartland of the old Hohenstaufen domains by conquering Nuremberg and Freiburg. Requires stability and the Ducal Restoration path.

conditions.text: Swabia follows the path of Ducal Restoration
Own Nuremberg, or a subject owns it
Own Freiburg, or a subject owns it
Stability at least 25

event.title: The Stauferreich Reborn
event.text:
The banner of the Hohenstaufen flies once more over Nuremberg's castle and the towers of Freiburg. What the last Staufer emperors lost through the chaos of the Interregnum, a new Swabian duke has reclaimed through steel and statecraft.

Franconia's imperial cities and the Breisgau's fertile lands now answer to Stuttgart. The heartland is secured, but the true domains of Frederick Barbarossa and Frederick II stretched far beyond these borders, over the Alpine passes and into the rich plains of Lombardy.

options.text: The eagles return to their aeries

destiny.name: Alpine Dominion
destiny.text: Secure control over the Alpine passes by taking Innsbruck from the Habsburgs, while building a formidable army and earning the respect of your peers.

conditions.text: Own Innsbruck, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 50
Prestige at least 50

event.title: Lords of the Alps
event.text:
Innsbruck has fallen. The Habsburg seat in Tyrol (gateway to Italy, guardian of the Brenner Pass) now flies the Swabian eagle. Control of the Alpine passes gives Swabia strategic command over the trade and military routes connecting Germany to Italy.

The question is how to exploit this mountain dominion. Some counsel fortifying every pass and valley, making the Alps an impregnable bastion. Others argue that the wealth of the conquered territories should be mobilized to raise massive armies for the campaigns ahead: Milan and Prague still beckon.

modifiers.name: Alpine Fortifications
modifiers.text: Every pass, valley, and mountain stronghold has been fortified, making the Swabian heartland virtually impregnable.

options.text: Levy the mountain peoples for our wars

modifiers.name: Imperial Levies
modifiers.text: The conquered territories are organized to provide maximum military manpower, with every subject people contributing their quota to the Swabian army.

destiny.name: The Imperial Crown
destiny.text: Restore the full extent of Hohenstaufen power by conquering Milan and Prague, fielding a massive army, and building Stuttgart into a residence worthy of the crown.

conditions.text: Own Milan, or a subject owns it
Own Prague, or a subject owns it
Army size at least 75
We own Stuttgart and its development is at least 53

event.title: The Imperial Crown
event.text:
Milan kneels before the Swabian duke. Prague's ancient castle acknowledges a new master. From the Rhine to the Vltava, from the Alps to the plains of Lombardy, the domains of the Hohenstaufen have been restored, and surpassed.

This is a power not seen in Central Europe since Frederick II held court in Palermo and ruled from the Baltic to Sicily. The question now is what manner of empire this shall be. Some urge the duke to claim universal monarchy: to impose Swabian will on all of Christendom through force of arms. Others counsel a more measured approach: an imperial federation that binds diverse peoples through shared institutions and mutual obligation.

options.text: One crown, one will, one empire

modifiers.name: Universal Monarchy
modifiers.text: The Swabian duke claims dominion over all of Christendom, wielding military force as the primary instrument of statecraft.

options.text: An empire of many peoples, one law

modifiers.name: Imperial Federation
modifiers.text: Diverse peoples are bound together under Swabian authority through shared institutions, mutual obligation, and the promise of order.

units.name: Bundschuh Militia
units.text: Urban militia drawn from the guilds and citizenry of Swabian free cities, trained to defend their walls and liberties against noble aggression.

units.name: Kreisinfanterie
units.text: Professional infantry of the Swabian Imperial Circle, organized through the collective military obligations of the Circle's member states.

units.name: Swabian Reiter
units.text: Heavy cavalry drawn from the imperial knights of the Swabian cantons, fighting in the traditional mounted shock role.

units.name: Bundesknechte
units.text: Paid foot of the Swabian League, sent by each member according to its quota and armoured in Augsburg and Ulm harness. From such Swabian Knechte the first Landsknechte were raised.

units.name: Augsburg Bombard
units.text: Heavy siege artillery cast in Augsburg's renowned foundries, built with the same metalworking expertise that produced the finest armor in Europe.

buildings.name: Webhaus
buildings.text: A Swabian weaving hall where guild masters oversee the production of fustian and fine cloth, carrying on the textile traditions of Augsburg and Ulm.

buildings.name: Handelskontor
buildings.text: A trading office of the Swabian League network, coordinating commercial activity and representing the collective interests of allied merchants.

buildings.name: Fuggerhaus
buildings.text: A banking and counting house in the Fugger tradition, managing credit, exchange, and investment for Augsburg's merchant dynasties.

buildings.name: Zeughaus
buildings.text: A Swabian arsenal where Augsburg's metalworkers forge weapons and armor for the League's military forces.

buildings.name: Fuggerei
buildings.text: A social housing settlement modeled on Jakob Fugger's pioneering foundation in Augsburg, providing affordable homes to workers and artisans.

buildings.name: Formschneiderei
buildings.text: A workshop of block cutters and printers in the Augsburg manner, where pictures are cut in pearwood, printed beside the text, and coloured by hand.

where.text: Paper is produced in the location's market

buildings.name: Borsenhaus
buildings.text: A Swabian commodity exchange where merchants from across Europe trade goods, credit, and futures, anchoring Augsburg's position as the commercial capital of the continent.

buildings.name: Kaiserpfalz
buildings.text: An imperial palace complex in the Hohenstaufen tradition, serving as both the seat of government and a symbol of restored ducal authority over the old stem duchy.

list.name: Bundesrat des Schwäbischen Bundes
list.text: The federal council of the Swabian League, formed at the Diet of Esslingen on 14 February 1488. The Bundesrat sat in three colleges: princes, imperial cities, and the knights of Sankt Jörgenschild, with two (later three) Hauptleute as chief captains and equal numbers of councillors elected from each estate, expanded from eighteen to twenty-one by the renewals of 1496 and 1500. It fielded an army of thirteen thousand men, suppressed the Peasants' War of 1525, and held southern Swabia together against feud and confessional schism until the Reformation broke the League in 1534.

list.name: Schwäbischer Kreistag
list.text: The deliberating assembly of the Schwäbischer Reichskreis, one of the ten imperial circles created by Maximilian I in 1500. The Dukes of Württemberg and the Bishops of Konstanz served as kreisausschreibende Fürsten, summoning the Kreistag and chairing its sessions. After 1512 the Kreis enforced the verdicts of the Reichskammergericht; from 1530 it raised the imperial-army contingent; after 1555 it policed the Eternal Public Peace within its territory. Of the ten circles, the Swabian was reckoned the best organised, divided after 1563 into the four execution-quarters of Augsburg, Konstanz, Württemberg, and Baden.

conditions.text: Owns Konstanz

list.name: Tübinger Vertrag
list.text: The constitutional contract concluded between Duke Ulrich and the Württemberg Landtag at Tübingen on 8 July 1514, in the wake of the Armer Konrad rising against Ulrich's meat-and-wine consumption tax. The treaty bound the duchy to consult the estates of prelates, knights, and burgher Ehrbarkeit on extraordinary taxation, war, and territorial alienation, and granted all subjects the right of free emigration and lawful procedure in matters of life, limb, and honour. Historians have called it the Magna Carta of Württemberg. It remained the territorial constitution, almost unchanged, until the Napoleonic mediatisation of 1805.

list.name: Reichsritterschaft Schwabens
list.text: The Swabian Imperial Knights' Congregation, formed between 1541 and 1545 from the dissolved Sankt Jörgenschild and organised into five cantons: Donau, Hegau-Allgäu-Bodensee, Neckar-Schwarzwald, Kocher, and Kraichgau. Each canton was governed by a Direktorium under a Ritterhauptmann elected for life, with elected Ritterräte; the cantons exercised taxation rights and military sovereignty over their subjects, and sold knightly estates only to other knights to keep the Ritterschaft territorially intact. The Swabian knights were the densest knightly corporation in the Reich and survived, immediate to the Emperor, until mediatisation in 1805/06.

list.name: Augsburger Stadtrat
list.text: The patrician-and-guild civic government of Augsburg, free imperial city since 9 March 1276. Until 1548 the Rat sat under a Zunftverfassung guaranteeing the guilds the majority over the patricians; the Welser, Höchstetter, Herwart, Baumgartner, and Fugger merchant houses sat alongside the artisan guilds and the Stadtpfleger. After the Peace of Augsburg of 1555 a confessionally mixed Catholic-Lutheran council presided over a majority-Protestant population. The Augsburger Stadtrat was the institutional engine of the south-German banking trade (the Fuggers' private cash routinely lent to emperors) until the Thirty Years' War broke it.

conditions.text: Owns Augsburg
